Neural ODE Training with Backpropagation Through Time (PyTorch)

This notebook converts week_4/scripts/torch/NODE_BPTT_vanilla.py and week_4/scripts/torch/NODE_BPTT_tuned.py into one interactive app. Design goal: start from the vanilla setup, then progressively enable tuning options. Navigation: Jump to Control Panel

1. Continuous-Time Model and BPTT Objective

True system: ||[x(t)=\begin{bmatrix}u(t)\\v(t)\end{bmatrix}, \quad \dot{u}=v, \quad \dot{v}=-\beta v - \frac{g}{\ell}\sin(u).||]Learned NODE: ||[\dot{x}=f_\theta(x), \qquad x_{k+1}=\Phi_\theta(x_k,\Delta t).||]Observations are generated by simulating the true dynamics and adding noise: ||[x^{\mathrm{obs}}_{k,m}=x^{\mathrm{true}}_{k,m}+\eta_{k,m}.||]Training objective: ||[\mathcal{L}(\theta)=\frac{1}{NM}\sum_{k,m}\|x^{\mathrm{sim}}_{k,m}-x^{\mathrm{obs}}_{k,m}\|_2^2 + \lambda\,\mathcal{R}(\theta).||]Optional regularization (tuned mode): ||[\mathcal{R}(\theta)=\frac{1}{\operatorname{mean}\|f_\theta(x)\|_2+\varepsilon}.||]Optional normalization used in the tuned script: ||[\tilde{x}=\frac{x-\mu_{\mathrm{obs}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{obs}}+\varepsilon}.||]BPTT differentiates through all RK4 steps. In discrete adjoint form: ||[a_k = a_{k+1}\frac{\partial \Phi_\theta}{\partial x_k} + \frac{\partial \ell_k}{\partial x_k}, \qquad \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}=\sum_k a_{k+1}\frac{\partial \Phi_\theta}{\partial \theta}.||]

1.1 Code: Loss Terms and Training Update

The next cell implements: ||[\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{data}}=\frac{1}{NM}\sum_{k,m}\|x^{\mathrm{sim}}_{k,m}-x^{\mathrm{obs}}_{k,m}\|_2^2,||]||[\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{data}}+\lambda\mathcal{R},||]||[\theta \leftarrow \theta - \alpha \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L},||]with optional weight decay, gradient clipping, and plateau LR scheduling.

3. Control Panel

Vanilla baseline (default):
  • Keep Use regularization term off.
  • Keep data normalization, weight decay, LR scheduler, and gradient clipping off.
  • Use hidden_dim=64, lr=5e-2, epochs=501.
How to tune toward the tuned setup:
  1. Turn on Use regularization term and start with reg_strength = 0.01.
  2. If trajectories become overly flat, increase reg_strength; if training destabilizes, decrease it.
  3. Then optionally turn on normalization, He initialization, weight decay (1e-4), scheduler, and clipping.
  4. Reduce learning rate (1e-2 or 5e-3) if oscillatory; increase epochs if still improving.
